$comment: Mission 1.64. The precondition, the approved-enquiry hash verification under three hashing boundaries, and the retrieval ledger.
mission: 1.64 — Anchor Enquiry Dispatch & ONYPHE Residual Closure V1

approved_enquiry_hash_verification.$comment: Section A1. The hashing boundary is documented rather than assumed, because a hash whose boundary nobody wrote down is a hash two readers can disagree about.

boundaries_tested.boundary: raw bytes as stored on disk

approved_enquiry_hash_verification.why_all_three_agree: The file is stored LF-only, so the three boundaries collapse to the same byte sequence. That is worth recording rather than assuming: on a Windows working tree a CRLF rewrite would have split them, and a mission that had tested only one boundary would not have known which one the approval named.
approved_enquiry_hash_verification.the_recipient_is_outside_the_frozen_rang: The frozen document records the recipient as TO_BE_SUPPLIED_BY_OPERATOR. Writing a real address into it would change its bytes and void the approval, so the address travels in the dispatch packet beside the document rather than inside it.

documentation_ledger.$comment: Part B only. Three targets, six retrievals.

requests.sought: whether a datascan category section exists beside the ctiscan one
what a single result represents and whether repeated scans append or update
how many results are returned per asset and whether they span time
per-field retention annotations naming which fields are dropped after thirty days
the complete function list, and any de-duplication or latest-only function
whether a summary aggregates several observations per asset

request_accounting.the_documentation_carried_examples: The API pages print illustrative outputs including example timestamps. They were read as field documentation and used for no analytical purpose, and no query was issued to obtain any.
